references.text: Samson's mother was told that no razor should come upon her son's head, for he was to be a Nazirite of God from the womb.
Samson explained that his strength was tied to the fact that no razor had ever touched his head, because he was a Nazirite of God.
Hannah made a vow that no razor should come upon Samuel's head if the Lord gave her a son.
The verse describes the Nazirite as holy to the Lord for all the days of their separation as a Nazirite.
At the end of the Nazirite period, the Nazirite was to shave their consecrated head at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
The priests were also not to shave their heads, showing the parallel between priestly and Nazirite holiness.
Ezekiel describes rules for the priests' hair, reflecting similar holiness requirements as those for the Nazirites.
Paul cut his hair in Cenchreae because he had a vow, likely a Nazirite vow.
Paul was asked to purify himself along with four men who had taken a vow, a reference to Nazirite practice.
